key_insight: Turbulence changes ice-crystal alignment and scattering, so assuming perfectly horizontal crystals can underestimate ice-water content.
engineering_relevance: Orientation-aware scattering models can help reduce biases in polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter ice-cloud retrievals.
method: Model overdamped spheroid orientations using settling-induced torque, turbulent gradients, rotational diffusion and intermittency.
Couple orientation statistics to Rayleigh, Rayleigh–Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering through Legendre moments.
Assess retrieval biases and compare predicted lidar signatures with exploratory EarthCARE observations.
evidence_signal: Combining specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits bias to 25% for single-size populations of the studied shapes; exploratory EarthCARE data show the predicted lidar signature most often near −11°C.
watch_item: The 25% bound can fail for size distributions spanning the alignment transition, and degree-scale tilt widths require crystals near or beyond the model’s validity range.
paper_title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
